title: Representing a connecting map and attaching the top projective term
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the module universe and let $C$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Work in $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(C)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ with localization $Q$, cochain shifts and cones [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix integers $a<b$, an object $P\in\mathcal A$, an object $M\in D(\mathcal A)$, and a complex $Q^\bullet$ which is zero outside $[a,b-1]$ and has projective terms (maps from each term lift along epimorphisms). Suppose a distinguished triangle is given:
$$P[-b]\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Q(Q^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\delta}P[-b+1].$$
Write $P[-b+1]$ also for the actual single-term complex with $P$ in degree $b-1$. There is a chain map $g:Q^\bullet\to P[-b+1]$ representing $\delta$ in the derived category. Its only possibly nonzero component is $g^{b-1}:Q^{b-1}\to P$, and it satisfies $g^{b-1}d_Q^{b-2}=0$. The complex $D^\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(g)[-1]$ represents $M$. Under the evident term identifications it has terms $Q^q$ for $q<b$, term $P$ in degree $b$, and zero terms outside $[a,b]$; with the cone differential $d_{\operatorname{Cone}(g)}(y,x)=(d_Ty+g(x),-d_Qx)$ for $T=P[-b+1]$, its last differential is $-g^{b-1}$. Negating the identification of the degree-$b$ term with $P$ gives the isomorphic attached complex with last differential $g^{b-1}$. In particular, if $P$ and all $Q^q$ are finite free $C$-module sheaves, then so are all terms of $D^\bullet$. The rank-zero case $P=0$ is included. No constancy of entries of $g^{b-1}$ is required.

proof.text: Put $T=P[-b+1]$, the complex concentrated in degree $b-1$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(C)$ is abelian, since the site is small relative to the module universe. The given $Q^\bullet$ is bounded above by $b-1$ and all its terms are projective. Apply the surjectivity part of [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] with source $Q^\bullet$ and target $T$ to $\delta:Q(Q^\bullet)\to Q(T)$. A homotopy-category morphism is a homotopy class of actual chain maps, so choose a representative $g:Q^\bullet\to T$. Its image under localization is $\delta$. No assumption that the whole sheaf category has enough projectives is used.

source.place: Tag 064B, lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex; applied to the final connecting map in proetale.tex Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex

proof.text: Because $T^q=0$ for $q\ne b-1$, each component $g^q$ except $g^{b-1}$ is zero. The chain-map equation in degree $b-2$, namely $d_T^{b-2}g^{b-2}=g^{b-1}d_Q^{b-2}$, has zero left-hand side. It therefore says $g^{b-1}d_Q^{b-2}=0$. All other chain-map equations have both sides zero: the target is supported in one degree and $Q^b=0$. This is exactly the cocycle condition needed for the last differential.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, together with the definition of a morphism of complexes; proetale.tex Tag 09C3 final extension-by-one paragraph

proof.text: Write $A=P[-b]$, $B=Q(Q^\bullet)$ and $E=\operatorname{Cone}(g)$. By the cone-triangle clause of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $B\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]\to Q(E)\to B[1]$ is distinguished. Rotate the given triangle twice using (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. If its first two maps are $u:A\to M$ and $v:M\to B$, the resulting distinguished triangle is $B\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1]\xrightarrow{-u[1]}M[1]\xrightarrow{-v[1]}B[1]$. The identity maps on $B$ and $A[1]$ commute with the identical first arrow $\delta$. By (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category], they extend to a morphism of these two distinguished triangles, with third component $c:M[1]\to Q(E)$. The first two components are isomorphisms, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes $c$ an isomorphism. Apply the inverse shift equivalence and the shift comparison of $Q$ from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $M\cong Q(E)[-1]\cong Q(E[-1])$. Thus the actual complex $D^\bullet=E[-1]$ represents $M$.

source.place: Tags 0145 (derived-definition-triangulated-category), 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle), 014B (lemma-cone-triangle-unique-isomorphism), and 014Q (definition-distinguished-triangle); this spells out the triangulated-category argument in proetale.tex Tag 09C3 final paragraph

proof.text: Compute the shifted cone using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In coordinates reordered as $(x,y)\in Q^q\oplus T^{q-1}$, one has $D^q=Q^q\oplus T^{q-1}$ and $d_D^q(x,y)=(d_Q^qx,-g^qx-d_T^{q-1}y)=(d_Q^qx,-g^qx)$. For $q<b$, $T^{q-1}=0$, so $D^q$ identifies with $Q^q$. For $q=b$, $Q^b=0$ and $T^{b-1}=P$, so $D^b$ identifies with $P$. For $q<a$ or $q>b$, both summands vanish. Consequently the differentials below $b-1$ are those of $Q^\bullet$, the last differential is $-g^{b-1}$, and the degree-$b$ outgoing differential is zero. The only new square-zero equation is $(-g^{b-1})d_Q^{b-2}=0$, established in step 2. The map that is identity in all degrees below $b$ and $-\operatorname{id}_P$ in degree $b$ identifies this complex with the version having last differential $g^{b-1}$.

source.place: Tag 014E, definition-cone, and the cochain shift convention; proetale.tex Tag 09C3 last paragraph

proof.text: The term identifications in step 4 show directly that every term is one of the given $Q^q$, $P$, or zero. If those sheaves are finite free (isomorphic to a finite direct sum of copies of $C$), each term is finite free, taking the empty direct sum for zero. When $P=0$, the target $T$ and $g$ vanish, and the formula gives $D^\bullet\cong Q^\bullet$ with its original differential. When $Q^\bullet=0$, it gives $D^\bullet=P[-b]$. For $b=a+1$ the only possible differential is $-g^a:Q^a\to P$, so the same construction still applies. The construction only uses a morphism of sheaves $g^{b-1}$ and its chain-map equation, with no condition on locally constant matrix entries.
